Understanding Varicose Veins: What Are They?

Varicose veins are enlarged, twisted veins that usually occur in the legs due to weakened or damaged vein walls and valves. Veins carry blood back to the heart, and they rely on tiny one-way valves to keep blood flowing in the right direction. When these valves fail, blood can pool in the veins, causing them to bulge, stretch, and become varicose.

This condition can present with a variety of symptoms:

● Aching or heavy legs, especially after standing or sitting for long periods

● Swelling in the lower legs and ankles

● Throbbing or burning sensations

● Visible blue or dark purple veins

● Skin discoloration around the affected veins

● Leg cramps or restlessness, especially at night

● In severe cases, ulcers or open sores around the ankles

Though more common in older adults and women, varicose veins can affect anyone, particularly those with a family history of vein disorders, obesity, sedentary lifestyles, or professions that require long hours of standing.
